For this discretization, stability is obtained using corrected discrete memory functionals adapted to the variable-order fractional terms.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof correctly derives the displayed inequality, but its left-hand side contains 𝓔 = Θ − R, and no nonnegativity or lower bound for 𝓔 is established. In fact 𝓔 can be negative under Assumption assu:orders_bounds: with T = 1, τ = 0.01 and ν(t) = 0.6 + 0.3t (continuous, values in [0.6, 0.9] ⊂ (0,1)), for a sequence supported at k = 1 the coefficient of ½‖φ¹‖² in 𝓔_{φ,100} is b_{100,1} − Σ_{j≥2}(δ_{j,1})₊, where b_{100,1} = (1 − 0.99^{0.1})/Γ(1.1) ≈ 1.06·10⁻³ while δ_{2,1} = b_{2,2} − b_{1,1} ≈ 2.5·10⁻³ alone exceeds it (Σ(δ_{j,1})₊ ≈ 2.9·10⁻³). Hence 𝓔_{φ,n} < 0 is possible, the proven bound controls no norm of u_h^n, B_h^n (nor even the dissipation sum, since a negative 𝓔 can be arbitrarily large in magnitude), and the advertised stability of the discrete solution does not follow from the argument.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reprove stability by testing Problem prob:fully with (u_h^n, B_h^n) and combining Lemma lem:frac1 with the discrete fractional Grönwall machinery already in the paper (Lemma lem:check_frac_assump, Appendix A) to bound ‖u_h^n‖² + ‖B_h^n‖² by the data (restricting to α = β, or comparing both kernels to the α_*-kernel to handle α ≠ β); no hypothesis set under which the present 𝓔-based bound yields stability is identified.
issues.overall_effect: The stability of the fully discrete scheme claimed in the abstract, contribution (3), Section 2.3 and Theorem thm:stability is not established: the bounded functional can take negative values, so no bound on the discrete solution or its dissipation is obtained. No other labelled formal result relies on thm:stability.
issues.title: Stability theorem bounds a corrected memory functional that is not nonnegative
issues.why_classification: The displayed inequality is validly derived but proves materially less than the promised stability, and the needed nonnegativity of 𝓔 fails in general under the stated assumptions; a recognizably comparable stability bound is recoverable by a contained reproof reusing the paper's own Grönwall tools (with at most a limited weakening such as α = β), so the loss is contained rather than architectural.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof needs ‖r₁ⁿ‖, ‖r₂ⁿ‖ ≤ Cτ (the only source of the τ² term in R = I₂, entering via the estimate of (r₁ⁿ, ξ_uⁿ) and (r₂ⁿ, ξ_Bⁿ)), i.e. the L1 consistency bound of eq:frac_replacement. Bounding the L1 truncation error of the Caputo derivative requires second-order time regularity (e.g. ∂ₜ²u, ∂ₜ²B ∈ L^∞(0,T;L²)), but Assumption assu:regularity assumes only first-order time regularity, and eq:frac_replacement asserts O(τ) with no hypotheses on φ at all. Under the stated assumptions the O(τ) temporal rate is therefore unsupported (and not valid in the stated generality).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen Assumption assu:regularity by adding ∂ₜ²u, ∂ₜ²B ∈ L^∞(0,T;L²(Ω)²) (or an equivalent condition) and include (or cite for eq:frac_replacement) the standard L1 truncation estimate ‖rⁿ‖ ≤ Cτ uniformly in n.
issues.overall_effect: The temporal convergence rate of Theorem thm:convergence, and the corresponding convergence claims in the abstract and contribution (3), are not established under the stated hypotheses.
issues.title: O(τ) convergence rate rests on an L1 truncation bound not implied by the assumed regularity
issues.why_classification: The gap is load-bearing (the entire O(τ) rate rests on it) and its repair requires both a strengthened hypothesis, narrowing the stated regularity class, and a nontrivial standard truncation lemma absent from the paper; nevertheless the method, conclusion, rate and practical scope survive recognizably, which is more than minor but avoids major loss.

issues.failure_explanation: Subtracting the two problems and testing with (ξ_uⁿ, ξ_pⁿ, ξ_Bⁿ) produces, besides the displayed terms, (1/Re)(∇ψ_uⁿ, ∇ξ_uⁿ) from the viscous term and −(ψ_pⁿ, ∇·ξ_uⁿ) from the pressure term (the ξ_p part vanishes since (∇·ξ_uⁿ, q_h) = 0). By the stated Stokes projector these combine to ((1/Re) − 1)(∇ψ_uⁿ, ∇ξ_uⁿ), which is nonzero for Re ≠ 1 and is absent from eq:conv_step2. (The analogous magnetic term (1/Rm)(∇ψ_Bⁿ, ∇ξ_Bⁿ) vanishes by the Ξ_h projector, so only the velocity side is affected.) The displayed error identity is therefore not a valid consequence of the stated subtraction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing term into eq:conv_step2 and estimate it via Young's inequality (≤ ε‖∇ξ_uⁿ‖² + C‖∇ψ_uⁿ‖², absorbed into I₂), or redefine the Stokes projector with the 1/Re coefficient so the viscous and pressure projection-error terms cancel identically.
issues.overall_effect: The intermediate identity eq:conv_step2 in the proof of Theorem thm:convergence is incorrect as written; the final convergence estimate is unaffected once the omitted term is bounded in the standard way, since it is absorbable into the existing I₂-type terms.
issues.title: Error identity eq:conv_step2 omits the projection-error viscous and pressure terms
issues.why_classification: A forced local correction whose treatment mirrors the Young-type estimates already carried out for neighboring terms in the same proof; the theorem's conclusion, rate and scope are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the numerical implementation uses a divergence-cleaning step for the magnetic field after each time step
for the magnetic field the cleaning step reduces the divergence substantially over the whole time interval

issues.failure_explanation: With B_hⁿ = B̃_hⁿ − ∇φ_hⁿ, integration by parts gives (∇·B_hⁿ, ψ_h) = (∇·B̃_hⁿ, ψ_h) + (∇φ_hⁿ, ∇ψ_h) (periodic/no-flux). Making B_hⁿ weakly divergence-free therefore requires (∇φ_hⁿ, ∇ψ_h) = −(∇·B̃_hⁿ, ψ_h), i.e. Δφ_hⁿ = ∇·B̃_hⁿ. The stated equation has the opposite sign, so as printed (∇·B_hⁿ, ψ_h) = 2(∇·B̃_hⁿ, ψ_h): the cleaning step doubles the weak divergence instead of removing it, contradicting both its stated purpose and the reported post-cleaning divergence reductions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the sign on the right-hand side of eq:elliptic (or equivalently set B_hⁿ = B̃_hⁿ + ∇φ_hⁿ in eq:recalculated_B), turning the step into the standard H¹-orthogonal Hodge projection.
issues.overall_effect: The cleaning step as printed fails its input-output contract (divergence reduction), and the reported numerical divergence reductions in Figures fig:conv_div_errors and fig:orszag_div_errors and Table tab:orszag_optimal_stabilization are inconsistent with the printed equations.
issues.title: Divergence-cleaning Poisson problem is stated with the wrong sign and doubles the magnetic divergence
issues.why_classification: A single forced sign correction restores the intended construction; no theorem, proof, guarantee, or qualitative numerical conclusion is affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Increasing $\zeta$ from 50 to 2000 with $\chi=1$ reduces ${\displaystyle \max_{n}\lVert \nabla\cdot\mathbf{u}^{n}_{h}\rVert}$ from $1.35\times10^{-5}$ to $1.18\times10^{-6}$

issues.failure_explanation: The table claims these are the computed values of max_n‖∇·u_hⁿ‖ and the diagnostic deviations for (ζ, χ) = (50,1) and (100,1); all six entries of the two rows coincide to the displayed precision. Yet the same column changes by about 13% between ζ = 100 and ζ = 200 and scales like 1/ζ for ζ ≥ 200 (1.1755e−5, 4.7040e−6, 2.3524e−6, 1.1763e−6). The discrete solution depends smoothly (analytically) on the grad-div parameter ζ, so two distinct values of ζ cannot yield identical divergence maxima to five significant digits while neighboring parameter values differ substantially. At least one of the two rows misreports the computed data, and the prose value 1.35×10⁻⁵ quoted for ζ = 50 inherits the error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute or re-report the (50,1) (or (100,1)) row and correct the corresponding prose value.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative stabilization-sensitivity data in Table tab:orszag_optimal_stabilization, and the sentence quoting the ζ = 50 divergence value, are unreliable; the qualitative conclusions (divergence decreases with ζ; energies and enstrophies are insensitive to ζ, χ) are not affected.
issues.title: Stabilization table reports identical results for ζ = 50 and ζ = 100, contradicting its own parameter dependence
issues.why_classification: A local data-reporting correction; no theorem, proof, guarantee, or qualitative conclusion depends on the duplicated row.
